---
title: "How suggestions work"
description: "Shared mechanics of the bot suggestion workflows: when they run, what they review, and how their suggestions reach you."
---

Three workflows propose changes to your package instead of just checking
it: [author suggestions](authors-suggest.qmd) for `DESCRIPTION`,
[roxygen suggestions](roxygen-suggest.qmd) and
[test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd). They share how
their changes reach you. What happens inside the roxygen and test
workflows, step by step, is shown [under the hood](suggestions-internals.qmd).

## When they run and what they review {#what-gets-reviewed}

The workflows run on pull requests and, if your caller adds a `push`
trigger, on pushes to your working branches. Either way they review **only
what is new since their last run**:

| Event | Reviewed |
|---|---|
| A pull request is opened or reopened | everything the PR changes |
| Another push to an open PR | only the commits of that push |
| A push to a branch without a PR | only the commits of that push |
| The first push of a new branch | the commits that exist on no other branch |
| A schedule or manual run | the whole package: a [sweep](#sweeps) |

How far your branch is ahead of or behind `dev` doesn't matter. Two kinds
of commits are left out, because they aren't new work on your branch:

- **commits merged in from another branch**, e.g. when you merge `dev`
  into your branch to catch up: they aren't reviewed, and their authors
  aren't credited on your branch;
- **the bot's own commits**, e.g. after you merge its suggestion PR: it
  doesn't review its own suggestions again.

A `paths` filter in your caller decides whether a run starts at all, e.g.
only when files under `R/` changed. The examples on each page show both
triggers.

## Suggestions are pull requests, never direct commits

A bot never commits to your branch. When a workflow has something to
suggest, it

1. commits each changed file separately on a branch
   `bot-suggest/<kind>/<your branch>`;
2. opens a pull request from there **into your branch**;
3. on a PR, comments on it, e.g.

   > **Roxygen documentation suggestions** opened: #19 (into `feat/my-feature`)
   >
   > 2 changes applied · 1 not applied
   >
   > - `R/ds.wrapper.R`

   The other titles are "Test suggestions" and "Update contributors in
   DESCRIPTION".

You review the suggestion like any PR: merge it, edit it first, or close
it.

### One suggestion PR per branch

While a suggestion PR is open, further runs **add to it** instead of
opening another one:

- your new commits are merged into the bot's branch, and where both
  changed the same lines, **your version wins**;
- the new suggestions are added on top, and the PR description gets an
  "Update for …" section with that run's report;
- if you changed a file that already has a suggestion, it is reviewed
  again against your current code, and the new suggestion replaces the
  old one.

So you can push and keep working before you look at the suggestions.

The suggestion PR's description also records, invisibly, up to which
commit the bot has reviewed. That's how a run that was dropped or failed in
between is caught up.

The bot's branch is **rebuilt** instead (with a note in the PR) when your
branch's history was rewritten, e.g. by a rebase and force-push, or when
your new commits can't be merged into it automatically. Then it contains
only that run's suggestions. If you'd rather always have only the latest
run's suggestions, set the input `open-suggestion-pr: replace`.

::: {.callout-note}
## One gap, by design
GitHub keeps at most one waiting run per branch. If you push three times
within a few minutes while **no** suggestion PR is open, the middle push's
run can be dropped, and its files are only reviewed when they change
again or in a sweep. Nothing wrong is proposed; one review is missing.
:::

## Sweeps {#sweeps}

The roxygen and test workflows also review the **whole package**, meant
for a monthly schedule, and collect everything in one pull request:

- **A scheduled run** sweeps `dev`, since GitHub always starts a schedule
  on the default branch (usually `main`).
- **A manual run** ("Run workflow") sweeps the branch you choose in the
  menu.
- **The `sweep-base` input** sets a fixed branch for both, e.g.
  `sweep-base: main` in a repository without `dev`.

The pull request goes into that branch, from
`bot-suggest/<kind>-sweep-<branch>-YYYY-MM`. Running a sweep again in the
same month updates that month's pull request. The test workflow limits
each sweep to recently changed functions plus a rotating share of the rest,
see [sweep scope](test-suggest.qmd#sweep-scope).

The mode follows the trigger by itself (`scan-mode: auto`, the default), so
one caller file handles pull requests, pushes and sweeps.

GitHub stops scheduled workflows in repositories without activity for 60
days. Add the [workflow keepalive](workflow-keepalive.qmd) so the sweeps
keep running.

## What gets proposed {#what-gets-proposed}

A suggestion should be a real improvement, not a reworded sentence or an
extra test for its own sake. So Claude has to state a **reason** for every
change, from a fixed list, and only some reasons lead to a proposal:

| Workflow | Proposed | Dropped |
|---|---|---|
| Roxygen | `missing`, `inaccurate`, `incomplete` | `clarity`, `style` |
| Tests | `uncovered_branch`, `error_handling`, `edge_case`, `regression` | `other` |

On top of that, the workflows drop documentation changes that differ only
in whitespace, punctuation or case, and tests whose assertions already
exist. The lists are set as `accept_reasons` in `config/claude.yml` and can
be [changed per repository](#adjusting-the-guidance). They are a first
setting, likely to be tuned.

The test workflow also changes **existing tests**, but only for fixed
reasons: an update when the function's behaviour was changed on purpose
(`contract_changed`), a deletion for a duplicate, removed behaviour or a
trivial test. A test that fails because the code may be wrong is only
reported. See [existing tests](test-suggest-review.qmd#existing-tests).

## Housekeeping

- **The bot never reviews itself:** runs on a `bot-suggest/*` branch are
  skipped, for pull requests and pushes alike.
- **Some runs do nothing, with a notice in the log:**
  - branch deletions and tag pushes;
  - pull requests from forks and from Dependabot, which get no secrets.
- **Runs of the same branch take turns:** a push run and a PR run for one
  branch never write the suggestion branch at the same time.
- **Cleanup:** [Cleanup suggestion branch](cleanup-suggestion-branch.qmd)
  deletes a `bot-suggest/*` branch once its pull request is merged or
  closed.
- **Checks on suggestion PRs:** with the
  [GitHub App](getting-started.qmd#github-app) configured, your required
  checks run on suggestion PRs; without it they don't, and a ruleset
  requiring them would block the merge.

## Adjusting the guidance

The workflows read their settings, guidance and prompts from this
repository. To change one for your package only, put a file at the **same
path** in your repository. It is used instead of the shared one:

| File | Controls |
|---|---|
| `config/bot-authors.json` | Accounts never added to `DESCRIPTION`, and how the bot recognises its own commits |
| `config/claude.yml` | Claude model, request settings and `accept_reasons` |
| `config/report-style.yml` | Heading levels and spacing of the suggestion reports |
| `config/roxygen-style.json` | Roxygen tag order and per-tag guidance |
| `config/test-categories.json` | Meanings of test file categories (`test-<category>-<function>.R`), see [test files](test-suggest.qmd#test-files) |
| `config/test-role-guidance.json` | Testing strategy given to Claude |
| `config/workflow-outcomes.yml` | What workflows produce, for the [workflow graphs](workflow-graphs.qmd) |
| `prompts/*.md` | The full prompts sent to Claude |

Start from a copy of the shared file, since yours replaces it completely.
(The [analysis scripts](datashield-analysis-suggest.qmd) workflow works
differently: its two settings files are merged key by key.)
